question: For the system $x+ky=1$ and $2x+4y=2$, determine the number of solutions when $k=2$ and when $k\ne2$.
explanation:
Coefficient determinant
The coefficient determinant is $$ egin{vmatrix}1&k\2&4\end{vmatrix}=4-2k$$
Case $k e2$
If $k e2$, then $4-2k e0$. Therefore, the coefficient matrix is nonsingular and the system has exactly one solution.
Case $k=2$
The equations become $x+2y=1$ and $2x+4y=2$. The second equation is exactly twice the first equation.
Classification
Hence, the system has infinitely many solutions when $k=2$ and a unique solution when $k e2$. There is no value of $k$ for which this system has no solution.

options.A: For $k=2$, there is no solution; for $k\ne2$, there are infinitely many solutions.
options.B: For $k=2$, there is a unique solution; for $k\ne2$, there are infinitely many solutions.
options.C: For $k=2$, there is a unique solution; for $k\ne2$, there is no solution.
options.D: For $k=2$, there are infinitely many solutions; for $k\ne2$, there is a unique solution.
